The eldest Zhang son had knelt before the Buddha for five days. He was filled with regret. 
Regret that he taught his younger brother swordsmanship but not how to protect himself while using it. 
So when his brother took a blade to champion justice, a moment's lapse left him gravely wounded—all the elder brother's fault. 

The monk entered the hall again, placing a piece of dark iron before him. 
Your brother lives, and there is still time. More knowledge brings more wisdom. You did nothing wrong—you simply did not do enough. 

He touched the iron. A servant rushed in with news: his younger brother had awoken. Overjoyed, he stumbled to his feet and ran out. 
I will teach him still—everything I know, one thing at a time. When full-fledged, he will ride the wind to places I could never reach.

Farming is the foundation of the nation, no task is more important. Throughout history, it was forbidden to slaughter oxen. Only after they died naturally could their meat, hide, tendons, or horns be used. During the Five Dynasties period, the monsoon line shifted south, prompting the migration of water buffalo southward. Thus, after Emperor Taizong's reign, the north had mostly yellow ox while the south had water buffalo. Additionally, folk paintings flourished in the Song era, and images of cattle frequently appeared in artworks such as Herding Cattle and Weaving and Farming Scenes.
